title: ReCal3R single scene-state write sensitivity screen

settings.model: Official ReCal3R code with the official final CUT3R checkpoint at 512-pixel input resolution
settings.stream_processing: ReCal3R processes an ordered image stream. For each image, it first predicts the current geometry and then selectively blends newly inferred information into a latent scene representation carried to later images.
settings.dataset: TUM RGB-D Freiburg3 walking recordings: static, xyz, rpy, and halfsphere
settings.sampling: Thirty-two images per recording, sampled deterministically and uniformly in natural temporal order
settings.comparison: The same prefix, write-target image, current output, pose memory, and known auxiliary state are shared. Only the post-output scene-state write for the write-target image is normal or disabled.
settings.measurement: The next uniformly sampled image is evaluated before that image writes to memory.

alignment.fit_scope: The common early prefix, sampled images 2–9
alignment.reuse: The fitted alignment is reused for both conditions.

settings.valid_pixels: Ground-truth-defined valid pixels shared by both conditions
settings.training_or_adaptation: No training, fine-tuning, optimization, or post-processing

event_table_scope.camera: Camera-error values are intentionally omitted because camera was not part of the continuation endpoint.
event_table_scope.signed_effect_definition: (error when the write is disabled - normal-write error) / normal-write error × 100
event_table_scope.sign_interpretation: Positive means the normal write reduced next-image error; negative means disabling the write reduced next-image error.

frozen_continuation_rule.aggregation: Within each recording and condition, average the two raw errors first, then take the absolute relative change between the condition means.
frozen_continuation_rule.recording_pass: A recording passes when either depth AbsRel or aligned 3D point error exceeds its endpoint threshold.
frozen_continuation_rule.experiment_pass: Continue to the full allocation experiment only when at least three of four recordings pass.
frozen_continuation_rule.interpretation: The 1% value is a pilot continuation threshold. It is not a significance test, a practical-equivalence margin, or proof of no effect.

checks: Pose memory and known auxiliary state matched across conditions.
The instrumented path matched the official recurrent path.
Identical-condition repeats stayed at the numerical floor.
Restoring a saved state reproduced uninterrupted output.
The ground-truth-defined valid mask matched across conditions.
The write-target image's current output matched across conditions.
A deliberately mistimed saved state produced a detectable difference.

rerun_agreement.qualitative_arrays: Every array element was reproduced exactly.
rerun_agreement.scope: This is computational reproducibility from a same-pipeline rerun, not external replication.

qualitative_selection.selection_rule: Selected post hoc as the event with the largest positive depth effect.

unrun_conditions: Scene-state write crossed with a pose-memory intervention

claim_boundaries.strongest_supported_claim: In these four 32-image sparse substreams and eight interventions, the recording-average first-next-sampled-image effect of one scene-state write on depth and aligned 3D point error stayed below the predeclared 1% continuation threshold, while leverage was not uniform over time.
does_not_support: Any unrun condition had a null result.

limitations: Only four related recordings and eight events were evaluated.
Averaging over all ground-truth-valid pixels may dilute local effects.
Only one write and the next sparse sample were evaluated.
Natural visibility, overlap, and motion were not controlled across events.
Only one checkpoint and the same compute path were used.
Camera was outside the continuation gate.
The qualitative case was selected post hoc.
The full allocation and pose-memory experiments were not run.
A known-state allowlist does not prove the absence of every possible mutable state.
next_question: Can high-leverage observations be constructed or predicted by controlled 3D evidence novelty, occlusion, and future revisit demand?
